title: End-to-End Finance Controls: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition (2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines Redwood Inference's end-to-end finance controls for budgeting and forecasting, contract intake and legal review, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition & billing. It consolidates policy, approval thresholds, operational runbooks, and templates required to maintain compliance, support accurate monthly close, and enable predictable financial planning.

Scope
Applies to all business units, international subsidiaries, and product teams that commit budget, sign contracts, purchase goods/services, or generate revenue. This includes: hosted API, Dedicated contracts, Private deployments, and professional services engagements.

Owners & Roles
- Finance (Primary owner): Controller, Revenue Accounting, FP&A
- Legal: Contract review, redline ownership for customer-facing agreements
- Procurement: Purchase order (PO) creation, vendor onboarding, supplier management
- Sales/BD/Product: Contract negotiation and commercial terms intake
- Engineering/Infra: Capital requests for hardware and software licenses

High-level Controls and Principles
- Segregation of duties: Requestors (product/engineering/sales) cannot approve their own spend beyond designated thresholds.
- Two-party approvals for spend over $25,000 (see thresholds below).
- Contract review required for any agreement that: contains data processing terms, indemnities, termination for convenience, SOC/ISO requirements, or payment > $50k/year.
- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles: identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, recognize when performance obligations are satisfied.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting
1.1 Annual Budget Cycle (timeline)
- Planning kickoff: Nov 1 - Finance issues guidance and templates
- Budget submission: Dec 15 - each department submits FY budget by line item
- Finance review & consolidation: Jan 1-31
- Board review & approval: Feb 15
- Operational reforecast cadence: monthly (rolling 12-month), with deep-reforecast each quarter (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4)

1.2 Templates & Required Inputs
- Headcount plan (FTE by role and hire month)
- Opex (SaaS, third-party services, cloud spend broken out by product/route)
- Capex requests (hardware purchases, capitalized development) with useful life and depreciation schedule
- Revenue by product line (hosted API, Dedicated, Private, professional services)
- Assumptions sheet (ARPU, churn, ARR conversion rates, customer acquisition cadence)

1.3 Approval Matrix (Budget commitments)
| Amount (USD) | Approver(s) | Additional Requirements |
|--------------:|------------|-------------------------|
| <= 10,000 | Dept Manager | Local PO if required |
| 10,001 - 25,000 | Dept Head + Finance FP&A | Budget owner sign-off |
| 25,001 - 100,000 | Dept Head + Finance Director | Procurement review |
| > 100,000 | CFO + Dept Head + Legal (if contract) | Board notification for > $250k |

1.4 Forecasting Controls
- Monthly rolling forecast must reconcile to GL by account.
- Material variances (> 10% or > $250k) require root cause analysis and corrective actions documented in the forecasting tool.

2) Contract Lifecycle & Legal Process
2.1 Contract Intake Steps
1. Sales/BD opens a Contract Intake form in the Contract Management System (CMS) with: customer name, contract type (SaaS/Dedicated/Private/PS), target term, list price, discounts, invoicing cadence, and security/compliance requirements.
2. Generate initial SOW/Order Form from approved template.
3. Route to Legal for redline.

2.2 Legal Review Triggers
- Any contract with non-standard indemnity, data residency requirements, or IP assignment.
- Contracts with payment terms > 60 days or prepayment clauses.
- Contracts involving export-controlled data or on-prem installs.

2.3 Standard Review SLAs
- Standard template modifications: 3 business days
- Non-standard / high-risk contracts: 7-10 business days
- Expedited requests: 24-48 hours with Product/Legal on-call (used rarely)

2.4 Signature and Storage
- Executed contracts must be stored in the CMS (DocuSign integration) with tagged metadata: customer, effective_date, term, ARR, renewal_terms, and assigned account owner.

3) Procurement Procedures
3.1 Purchase Types
- Opex: cloud credits, SaaS tools, contractor services.
- Capex: servers, GPUs, on-prem appliances, capital software licenses.

3.2 Vendor Onboarding Checklist
- Vendor information: legal name, W-9/W-8, certificates of insurance (where applicable), contact info, and bank details.
- Security assessment: for vendors accessing customer data or internal systems (run by Security Team).
- Tax and compliance checks: Procurement verifies applicable tax treatments and local compliance.

3.3 PO & Approval Flow
- Requestor submits requisition in Procurement system with supporting quotes and budget code.
- Procurement validates vendor and issues PO upon approvals per the Approval Matrix.
- Goods/services may not be ordered without an approved PO unless covered by corporate card policies.

3.4 Thresholds and Approvers (Procurement)
- <= $5,000: Dept Manager approval (no PO required for recurring subscription renewals if within budget).
- $5,001 - 25,000: Dept Head + Procurement
- $25,001 - 100,000: Procurement Director + Finance Director
- > $100,000: CFO + Procurement Director + Legal if contract accompanies purchase

3.5 Competitive Bidding
- For purchases > $50,000, require at least two competitive quotes unless an approved single-source justification is documented and approved by Procurement Director.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy (Summary)
4.1 Principles
- Revenue recognition is governed by ASC 606 (or local equivalent). Primary steps: identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize revenue when obligations are satisfied.

4.2 Product-specific guidance
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as tokens are consumed (variable consideration). Record invoiced recurring minimums as deferred revenue and recognize over the contract period.
- Dedicated (capacity-based): Recognize ratably over the contracted period when capacity is available and customer has the ability to use it.
- Private deployments & professional services: Split between deliverable-based obligations (e.g., deployment) recognized at completion of milestone and ongoing support recognized ratably over support term.

4.3 Billing & Invoicing Practices
- Standard invoices: Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated.
- Prepaid contracts: Record cash received as deferred revenue and recognize in accordance with performance obligations schedule.
- Usage reconciliation: For usage-billed customers, generate monthly usage reports; apply estimated true-ups on the following invoice when material (>5% variance or > $1,000).

4.4 Deferred Revenue & Journal Entries (example)
- On receipt of prepayment: Dr Cash / Cr Deferred Revenue (liability)
- Monthly recognition: Dr Deferred Revenue / Cr Revenue
- When invoicing usage: Dr Accounts Receivable / Cr Revenue (and if prepayment applied, clear deferred revenue)

4.5 Revenue Cutoff Controls
- All contract amendments, addenda, or renewals must be captured in the CMS and reconciled monthly to the billing system.
- Close-period lock: No revenue adjustments allowed after lock without Controller sign-off and documented supporting evidence.

5) Controls, Monitoring, and Auditability
- Monthly close checklist (owned by Controller): revenue reconciliation between billing system, CMS, and GL; deferred revenue roll-forward; high-risk contract list.
- Quarterly internal audit: sample contracts, POs, and vendor onboarding files.
- External audits: maintain evidence for ASC 606 compliance, SOC2 reports for vendors, and banks/receipt confirmations for major receipts.

6) Operational Runbooks & Checklists
6.1 FP&A Close & Forecast Runbook (monthly)
1. Pull actuals from GL by account and product code.
2. Reconcile billings and cash receipts to AR ledger.
3. Update rolling forecast with closed month actuals and document material variances.
4. FP&A sign-off and distribution to execs by 5th business day.

6.2 Contract Execution Runbook
1. Ensure signed contract uploaded to CMS within 48 hours of signature.
2. Tag contract with revenue product code and billing owner.
3. If implementation required, create project in PSA and map milestones to revenue obligations.

6.3 Procurement Closeout Checklist
- Confirm services delivered and accepted (PO closure)
- Verify invoice matches PO/receipt and code to correct GL account
- Update vendor master if recurring

7) Templates & Examples (extracts)
- Contract intake template: customer_name, product_line, ARR, term_months, billing_cycle, security_requirements, PO_needed (Y/N)
- PO template: vendor, description, amount, account_code, delivery_date, approved_by
- Revenue allocation example (SaaS + implementation): total contract $120k = $20k implementation (one-time recognized at completion) + $100k support/service over 12 months ($8,333/month).

Appendix: Quick-reference approval matrix
- Budget approvals: see section 1.3
- Procurement approvals: see section 3.4
- Contract thresholds for Legal review: payment > $50k/year, non-standard terms, data processing clauses

Questions & escalation
For questions about policy interpretation, exceptions, or urgent contract reviews, contact: finance-legal@redwood.ai. For security vendor assessments, include security@redwood.ai in the intake.
